cards.text: King David has fled Jerusalem after hearing that the hearts of the men of Israel are with his son Absalom (2 Samuel 15:13-14). Now Absalom and all the men of Israel come into Jerusalem. And right there with him is Ahithophel, who was David's counselor (2 Samuel 15:12).
But when David fled, he sent his friend Hushai the Archite back to the city to thwart Ahithophel's counsel (2 Samuel 15:32-34). Now Hushai walks right up to Absalom.

cards.question: Hushai is undercover, standing face to face with Absalom. How does he greet him?

answers.text: He cheers for him as king

cards.text: Absalom is NOT sold. David's best FRIEND cheering at his door is like the rival company's top guy strolling into your office yelling, "I'm SO glad to be here!"

cards.question: Absalom pushes back on Hushai. What does he ask him?

answers.text: Why he didn't go with David
Why he came to the city so late
Why he showed up without a gift

cards.text: Hushai doesn't flinch. "Not at all," he says, and he tells Absalom he'll stick with whoever the LORD, this people and all the men of Israel have chosen.

cards.question: Hushai tells Absalom he'll serve him the same way he served his father David.

cards.text: Then Absalom turns to Ahithophel: "Give me counsel. What should we do?" Ahithophel tells him to sleep with his father's concubines, the ones David left to take care of the palace.

cards.question: Ahithophel says all Israel will hear that Absalom has become a stench to his father. What does he say that will do?

cards.text: So they pitch a tent for Absalom on the roof. And he sleeps with his father's concubines in the sight of all Israel.

cards.question: In those days, how did both David and Absalom regard Ahithophel's advice?

answers.text: Like consulting the word of God
Like a guess worth double checking
Like a rumor from the city gate

cards.text: And Ahithophel isn't done. He wants to choose twelve thousand men and go after David himself.

cards.question: Ahithophel wants to wait a few weeks before going after David.
Ahithophel says he'll throw David's people into a panic so they flee. Then he'll strike down only the ___.

cards.text: Then he'll bring all the people back to Absalom "as a bride returning to her husband." One target, quick and clean, and honestly, friend? I do NOT love how good this plan sounds.

cards.question: Ahithophel tells Absalom he seeks the life of only one man. Then all the people will be at ___.
Ahithophel's plan doesn't sit well with Absalom and the elders of Israel.

cards.text: Then Absalom says, "Summon Hushai the Archite as well, and let us hear what he too has to say." The man David sent back to wreck this plan just got INVITED to the meeting!

cards.question: Absalom lays out Ahithophel's plan and asks Hushai if they should carry it out. Hushai says Ahithophel's advice is sound this time.

cards.text: Hushai reminds Absalom that David and his men are mighty men, as fierce as a wild bear robbed of her cubs. A BEAR, friend, and I can't even step off my own base to run.

cards.question: Hushai calls David a man of war. Who does he say David won't spend the night with?
Hushai says that by now David is probably hiding in a cave or some other place.

cards.text: Then Hushai paints a picture: some of Absalom's troops fall first, and word gets around.

cards.question: Hushai says whoever hears of it will say there's been a ___ among the troops who follow Absalom.

cards.text: Once that spreads, Hushai says, even the bravest soldier with the heart of a lion will melt with fear. Why? Because all Israel knows David is a mighty man with valiant men beside him.

So Hushai's plan is to gather all Israel from Dan to Beersheba, a multitude like the sand on the seashore. Ahithophel asked for twelve thousand men, and Hushai wants EVERYBODY, which is like trying to get the whole family into one group photo.

cards.question: In Hushai's plan, who should lead all Israel into battle?

cards.text: Hushai says they'll descend on David like dew on the ground, and not one of his men will remain. Friend, Hushai is SELLING this thing like a late-night TV ad.

cards.question: Hushai says that if David retreats to a city, all Israel will drag that city down into the valley.
Absalom and all the men of Israel have heard both plans. They say the advice of ___ is better.

cards.text: So Hushai's plan wins the room. But the passage tells us Who was really behind it.

cards.question: Why does Ahithophel's advice get turned down?

answers.text: The LORD purposed to thwart it

cards.text: And look closely: the text still calls Ahithophel's counsel good. Then Hushai goes to Zadok and Abiathar, the priests, and tells them both plans.

cards.question: Hushai tells the priests to send word to David quickly. What's the message?

answers.text: Cross over and don't stay the night
Hide in a cave and wait it out
Come back and fight Absalom now

cards.text: Meanwhile, Jonathan and Ahimaaz, the priests' sons, are staying at En-rogel (2 Samuel 15:27). A servant girl brings them news and they carry it to David, because they don't dare be seen entering the city.

cards.question: A young man spots Jonathan and Ahimaaz and tells Absalom.

cards.text: The two take off fast and reach a man's house in Bahurim. He's got a well in his courtyard.

cards.question: With Absalom's men after them, Jonathan and Ahimaaz climb down into the ___.
How does the man's wife hide the well?

answers.text: She covers it and scatters grain on top
She rolls a heavy stone over it
She stacks firewood all around it

cards.text: I spent YEARS under paper and dust in a junk drawer, so I respect a good hiding spot. Then Absalom's servants show up and ask her, "Where are Ahimaaz and Jonathan?"

cards.question: What does the woman tell Absalom's servants?
Absalom's servants search and find Jonathan and Ahimaaz.

cards.text: Once the men are gone, the two climb out of the well and go tell David. Their message: get up and cross the river at once, because Ahithophel has given advice against you.

cards.question: David gets the warning. What do he and all the people with him do?
By ___, there's no one left with David who hasn't crossed the Jordan.

cards.text: Now Ahithophel sees that his advice wasn't followed. He saddles his donkey.

cards.question: Where does Ahithophel ride off to once his advice isn't followed?

cards.text: There, he puts his affairs in order and hangs himself, and he's buried in his father's tomb. That's where we'll leave it for now, friend, because this story isn't over.

findings.problem: The card calls Hushai "David's best FRIEND." The text only calls him David's friend (2 Samuel 16:16-17). "Best" is stated as a fact, not kept inside the joke's comparison.

rule.text: Don't stretch the text. Exaggerate only in his own jokes.

findings.problem: No story card sets up 16:23, and only the right answer sounds like the Bible or speaks well of Ahithophel. The two wrong answers are dismissive ("a guess worth double checking," "a rumor from the city gate"), so they clash with card 1, which calls him David's counselor. The right answer stands out.

rule.text: Don't let the right answer stand out. All the answers should sound alike. None should sound more like the Bible, or more modern, than the others.

findings.problem: The question says Ahithophel will throw David's people into a panic. In 2 Samuel 17:2 he says he will throw David into a panic ("I will throw him into a panic"), and then the people with him will flee.

rule.text: Papa Dorin can retell in his own words and fill in what the text clearly implies. Scene-setting details are fine. He never says anything the text shows is wrong.

findings.problem: "The passage tells us Who was really behind it" uses a capital "Who," which points to God. That gives away card 15's answer ("The LORD purposed to thwart it") and rules out both wrong answers.

rule.text: A setup line can't rule out the wrong answers either.

findings.problem: Card 3 says the man has a well in his courtyard. Card 4 then asks where Jonathan and Ahimaaz climb down to, and the answer is "well," so the story card gives the answer away.

rule.text: No card ever gives away the answer to a choice card that comes later.

findings.problem: The line saying the story isn't over ("That's where we'll leave it for now, friend, because this story isn't over") is nearly a copy of the doc's example line instead of a new one.

rule.text: The examples show the idea. Write your own line each time.
